forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: No formal AGI declaration as of late May 2026; researcher consensus continues to drift toward late-2020s/early 2030s. Hassabis maintains ~50% by 2030; Amodei sees 2027 plausibility; OpenAI/Anthropic shipping major models but no AGI claim.
forecasts.base_rate: Prior expert median forecasts have clustered around 2030–2035. Historical AI timelines have consistently slipped. Only ~3.5 years of runway remain to end-2029.

factors_up.factor: GPT-5.4 hit record 83% on OpenAI GDPval; rapid frontier model cadence
Multiple lab CEOs publicly forecast AGI within 2–4 years
Resolution allows '3+ leading researchers state AGI achieved' — relatively low bar

factors_down.factor: No major lab has declared AGI; benchmark gains don't equal AGI consensus
Industry timelines have historically slipped; productivity/coding gains ≠ general cognition
Definitional ambiguity makes 3-researcher consensus harder than it sounds

key_uncertainties: Whether scaling continues to deliver capability gains through 2027–2029
Whether AI lab CEOs will use 'AGI' label commercially before researcher consensus
Definitional ambiguity around 'AGI' threshold
update_triggers: Any major lab declaring AGI achieved
Joint statement by 3+ leading researchers
Major capability breakthrough on long-horizon agentic tasks

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Morgan Stanley research shows UK consultant vacancies down 37% since ChatGPT launch — strongest evidence yet that AI is materially affecting consultancy demand. Tightens the case that ≥33% decline by 2030 is plausible, though resolution requires attribution by 2+ credible analyses.
forecasts.base_rate: Sector-wide 33%+ declines attributable to a single technology in <6 years are rare historically. Comparable: travel agents post-internet, retail post-Amazon — but those took longer.

factors_up.factor: UK vacancies for consultants down 37% since late 2022 (Morgan Stanley)
50% of UK execs expect AI to reduce total employment (up from 33%)
Early-career hiring (2–5 yrs) — the pyramid base of consultancies — most affected

factors_down.factor: Revenue and employment are distinct; firms may shrink headcount while sustaining revenue
Attribution requirement: 2+ credible analyses must blame AI specifically
Large incumbents (Big 4, MBB) are AI-adapting rapidly — may capture rather than lose value

key_uncertainties: Whether 'economic consultancy' is interpreted narrowly or broadly (Big 4, boutique econ consultancies, strategy)
Pace of AI capability advances in autonomous analysis through 2028–2030
Whether headcount declines translate into revenue/value declines
update_triggers: Major consultancy publishing AI-attributed headcount cuts
Industry revenue report showing >15% YoY decline
Credible analyst report quantifying AI-driven contraction

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Labour at 18.7% in latest polling moving average — sharply behind Reform UK (26.9%) and roughly tied with Conservatives (18.3%). Catastrophic May 2026 local elections (lost 38 councils). 95+ Labour MPs publicly questioning Starmer leadership.
forecasts.base_rate: Incumbent governments rarely recover from mid-term polling in the high teens to win the most seats. Comparable mid-term lows for governing parties typically presage seat losses, not pluralities.

factors_up.factor: FPTP can deliver largest-party status even with ~25–28% vote share if opposition splits
Up to ~3.5 years for recovery before December 2029 deadline
Leadership change could deliver 3–6pt bounce

factors_down.factor: Reform UK leading by ~8pts and gaining structural strength
Local election rout in May 2026 signals deep voter exodus
Internal party turmoil; Starmer under sustained pressure
Fragmented opposition could still allow Reform to win pluralities of seats

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform consolidates or peaks early
Election timing (PM-discretion before 2029)
Whether a Starmer replacement reorients Labour effectively
update_triggers: Labour leadership change
Reform polling collapse below 20%
Major Labour policy reset bouncing polls into mid-20s

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Maintained near prior. Long horizon and ongoing capability advances continue to support a high probability of AGI declaration by 2034. Multiple credible CEO claims push toward late-2020s, leaving large buffer.
forecasts.base_rate: Median expert and superforecaster timelines now cluster around 2030–2035 for transformative AI. Long horizons + accumulating capability + commercial incentive favour declaration.

factors_up.factor: Frontier models continue rapid capability gains (GPT-5.4 GDPval 83%)
Major lab leaders forecast AGI within 2–4 years — leaves 6–8 yr buffer
Resolution allows researcher-consensus path (low bar with 9 years runway)

factors_down.factor: Possible scaling plateau or compute/energy bottleneck
Regulatory or geopolitical disruptions could slow progress
'AGI' definition could harden, raising the bar for declaration

key_uncertainties: Whether scaling laws hold through 2030
Compute/energy constraints in late 2020s
Geopolitical disruption (AI export controls, war)
update_triggers: Evidence of a scaling plateau
Major regulatory clampdown
AGI-level capability demonstrations on agentic benchmarks

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Late-May 2026: 30-hour Chinese Coast Guard standoff at Pratas Island; PLA exercises near Taiwan. March 2026 US ODNI assessment: 'Chinese leaders lack fixed timeline or current plans for invading Taiwan'; favoured strategy is grey-zone coercion. Slight uptick from rising incident frequency but no evidence of imminent kinetic action.
forecasts.base_rate: Major-power amphibious assaults are historically rare events. Most analyst median timelines for serious Taiwan contingency are 2027–2030+; outright invasion remains tail-risk.

factors_up.factor: Pratas standoff and PLA exercises raise grey-zone temperature
Xi has reportedly directed PLA to be ready by 2027
Trump–Xi dynamic adds unpredictability

factors_down.factor: US ODNI assesses no fixed timeline; grey-zone preferred
PLA still building amphibious & joint-force readiness
Massive economic cost to China (Bloomberg/RAND: trillions in losses)
Blockade lasting >72hrs is a high bar — short shows-of-force won't resolve YES

key_uncertainties: Whether grey-zone coercion escalates into a sustained quarantine/blockade
Trump administration's Taiwan policy stability
Internal Chinese political pressures on Xi
update_triggers: Sustained PLA mobilization unlike training exercises
Major diplomatic break (e.g., US ambiguity collapse)
Xi public hardening of timeline

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: CPI at 2.8% (April 2026) and BoE base-case projection shows inflation rising to ~3.5% by end-2026, only returning near 2% in Q2 2027. New energy price-cap hike from July 2026 will push CPI further up. Almost no plausible path to a sub-2% monthly print between now and Dec 2026.
forecasts.base_rate: Six months of remaining data; current rate 0.8pp above target with rising trajectory. Sustained moves of >0.8pp in <6 months historically uncommon absent shock.

factors_up.factor: Energy price shock could reverse if Middle East tensions de-escalate fast
Wage growth weakening could pull services inflation down

factors_down.factor: BoE projects inflation rising not falling through 2026
Ofgem cap rises from July 2026 pushing utility costs up
Services inflation still sticky around 4%
Only 7 monthly prints remain to resolve YES

key_uncertainties: Trajectory of oil/gas prices into H2 2026
Pace of services inflation moderation
Sterling and import-price dynamics
update_triggers: Surprise CPI print below 2.3% in summer 2026
Collapse in energy prices
Major sterling appreciation

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Pre-release indicators remain extraordinary: 1B+ trailer views in <1 week, Polymarket 54.5% odds of being top 2026 domestic film, projected $2.54B worldwide. Slight haircut from prior 97% to reflect normal release-window execution risk.
forecasts.base_rate: Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021) grossed $1.9B; Holland-led MCU Spider-Man franchise has consistently exceeded expectations. ~25% of marquee MCU+Spider-Man releases since 2017 have cleared $1.5B.

factors_up.factor: Record-breaking trailer engagement (1B views <1 week)
5 months of theatrical runway from Jul 31 to Dec 31
Tracking projects ~$2.5B worldwide
Strong slot positioning vs other 2026 tentpoles

factors_down.factor: Standard release execution risk (reviews, word-of-mouth)
China release uncertainty for Marvel titles
Possibility of macro shocks or theatrical disruption

key_uncertainties: China release approval and box office contribution
Quality reception (Rotten Tomatoes / CinemaScore)
Competition from Avengers: Doomsday late 2026
update_triggers: Opening weekend below $200M domestic
China release ban
Critical reception below 60% Rotten Tomatoes

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Q1/Q2 2026 reporting confirms threshold already exceeded: Anthropic ARR ~$45B (CNBC, The Information), OpenAI ARR ~$33B = combined ~$78B. Question resolves YES barring revenue collapse before Q4 2026.
forecasts.base_rate: Once a question's threshold is mechanically crossed and resolution criteria are based on later reporting of the same trajectory, near-certain.

factors_up.factor: Combined Q2 2026 ARR ~$78B vs $70B threshold (already +11%)
Both firms showing strong sequential growth
Q4 2026 reporting window likely shows even higher numbers

factors_down.factor: ARR is a snapshot; massive churn could in principle reverse
Definitional/reporting ambiguity (which sources, which point in time)

key_uncertainties: Whether Q4 2026 disclosures align with current reporting
Whether 'combined ARR' nets out any inter-company API revenue (immaterial here)
update_triggers: Major customer loss event
Methodology change in reported ARR figures

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: OBR March 2026 EFO has medium-term real GDP averaging ~1.6% to forecast horizon, with downward productivity revisions (TFP 0.8% vs 1.1% earlier). AI contribution to productivity central case +0.2pp by horizon. 1.5% threshold is roughly at the OBR central case.
forecasts.base_rate: UK real GDP growth has averaged ~1.4% (2010s) and ~1.1% (2020-2024). Decadal average above 1.5% is roughly a coin-flip outcome given current trend.

factors_up.factor: AI productivity upside (OBR +0.2pp central, with upside scenarios)
OBR central case sits near 1.6%
Possible policy reforms (planning, immigration) under future governments

factors_down.factor: Downward TFP revisions; productivity disappointment risk
Debt at ~95% GDP early 2030s — fiscal drag risk
Demographic headwinds (aging, slower workforce growth)
Recession in any single year of 2030s would weigh heavily on decadal average

key_uncertainties: Magnitude and timing of AI productivity boost
Whether UK avoids deep recession over the decade
Government policy trajectory post-2029 election
update_triggers: New OBR long-term projections revising medium-term growth
Major productivity data revisions
UK recession in late 2020s changing entry point
